topic: Saturnus's desks: the police office, the lab, the meeting room, the izakaya, the bar and the back alleys

questions.text: When a model says it looked again at part of the image, what in its output would show that the second look changed the answer?
A cited sentence appears word for word in its source. What can the claim built on it still get wrong?
For a result you trust, what is one condition nobody ran, and where is that written down?

relations.purpose: At the records shelf, go through the nine failed experiments one at a time and note which path each finding closes, so the next person does not walk it again.
relations.reason: The item names police-office-1. Saturnus files failures the way the office files cases: closed, kept and findable. The beach holds the reading of the same archive.

relations.purpose: Open Snowdrop's open-threads case (OT-001) on the evidence board: three questions with no answer yet, from missing error bars to fading visual evidence. Pick the one you could bring a source to.
relations.reason: Open threads is a case file with clues, and the evidence board is where open cases hang. It is the one Snowdrop item that is a board of questions rather than a reading.

relations.purpose: At the audit console, run Saturnus's eight checks (seeds, config hash, data hash, leakage, baseline parity, negative controls, seed variance, what was not tested) against one result you already believe.
relations.reason: The hospital lab is Saturnus's audit room and the audit console is its terminal. The checklist is meant to be used, not read, so here it is a check. Door 305 keeps the reading.

relations.question: q-look-again
relations.purpose: On the method cart, read Snowdrop's deep read of V*: a model first judges whether the target is clearly visible, and if not, searches the high-resolution image before it answers.
relations.reason: The item names hospital-1. The method cart is the lab's terminal for methods, and V* is a method paper: a search step designed into the model.

relations.question: q-quote-or-claim
relations.purpose: At the project board under the audit card, take one claim and ask MingJing's question of it: does the quoted evidence appear word for word in the source it cites?
relations.reason: The audit card says a result needs a second look. The meeting room is where a claim is checked; the izakaya is where the MingJing note is read.

relations.question: q-quote-or-claim
relations.purpose: Read Saturnus's note on MingJing at the menu boards: the model proposes, code decides, a claim gets in only if its quote appears in the source, and the checker sees the evidence, never the argument.
relations.reason: The item names izakaya-1 (Nonbee). The menu boards are the izakaya's terminal; this is the reading place, the meeting room is the checking place.

relations.purpose: At last call, before a result is written up, tick Saturnus's six boxes against it: seed, config, library versions, data hash, best and last run, failed runs listed.
relations.limits: The checklist is a draft template; the bar holds no experiment to check it against.
relations.reason: The item names bar-1 (BarCosmos). Last call is the moment before closing; the checklist is the moment before writing up.

relations.purpose: Look over the junk stack behind the shut bar, sorted by someone who plans to come back, and follow Saturnus's short note to the Vault: failed runs are archived, not deleted.
relations.reason: The alley has no terminal. The junk stack is kept and sorted, not thrown away, which is what the note says of failed runs.

relations.question: q-untested
relations.purpose: Find the one empty outline in the open toolbox, then read Saturnus's check eight: write down what you did not test, and copy it into the limitations as it is.
relations.reason: The toolbox shows what is missing because its outline is drawn. Check eight asks for the same outline around what was not run.

relations.purpose: Read the full eight-item checklist on the resident notice. Its point is that a list does not get tired and does not skip an item because the result looks good.
relations.reason: Door 305 is Saturnus's checklist column and the resident notice is its terminal. This is where the checklist is read; the hospital console is where it is used.

relations.purpose: At the truck console, read the engineering-science manifesto: research kept as a trail of files, seeds and code that can be lit up again, and a field that was not measured written as null, never as zero.
relations.reason: The item names landfill-1. The landfill sorts what is kept from what is thrown out (the lidded bin is for keeping), the same line the manifesto draws for run records.

relations.purpose: At the guest book, use the distillation audit as a check on any reasoning trace: count real revisions, not words like wait or actually, and note where the two counts part.
relations.reason: This corridor is Saturnus's gaps column. The audit's finding is a gap between words and acts; the park holds the reading, this is the check.
